title: CatalogEx
description: CatalogEx service health: traffic, errors, and server-side latency from Prometheus; individual requests from Tempo.

panels.title: Scrape status
panels.description: Whether Prometheus scraped each CatalogEx pod on its last attempt (`up`). This shows that a scrape succeeded, not that the pod is ready. "No matching target data" means no target with these labels exists in this Prometheus for the selected filters; the cause is not shown here.

panels.title: Process uptime
panels.description: Time since each CatalogEx process started (`process_start_time_seconds`). A short uptime means the process restarted recently or the pod was replaced. This is not a Kubernetes restart count.

panels.title: Requests (range, estimated)
panels.description: Requests handled in the selected time range. `increase()` extrapolates across the range, so this is an estimate. Requests recorded before a series was first scraped, such as the first request after a restart, may be missing. Health checks, /metrics, and Swagger UI (/docs) are not counted.

panels.title: 5xx share (range)
panels.description: Share of requests in the selected range that returned a 5xx status. 0% means requests were handled and none failed with 5xx. "No traffic" means no requests were handled. "No matching data" means no request series match the filters. Red marks any 5xx; this is a visual cue, not an agreed SLO.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(http_request_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", app="catalogex", instance=~"$instance", route!~"/docs.*", statusCode=~"5.."}[$__range])) or vector(0)) / sum(increase(http_request_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", app="catalogex", instance=~"$instance", route!~"/docs.*"}[$__range]))

panels.title: 4xx share (range)
panels.description: Share of requests in the selected range that returned a 4xx status: validation errors, unsupported content types, products that were not found, and unknown paths. Check the route table and status chart to see which.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(http_request_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", app="catalogex", instance=~"$instance", route!~"/docs.*", statusCode=~"4.."}[$__range])) or vector(0)) / sum(increase(http_request_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", app="catalogex", instance=~"$instance", route!~"/docs.*"}[$__range]))

panels.title: p95 server-side duration (range)
panels.description: 95th percentile of server-side request duration over the selected range, across all routes and pods. It is measured inside the service, so network and router time are not included. It is estimated from histogram buckets, and with few requests it is close to the slowest request. Read it with the request count.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (increase(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", app="catalogex", instance=~"$instance", route!~"/docs.*"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Routes (selected range)
panels.description: One row per method and route template. Request counts are estimated with `increase()`. Shares are relative to that route's requests. A 5xx share above zero is red. p50 and p95 are server-side durations estimated from histogram buckets, and need several requests to mean much. "unmatched" groups requests to unknown paths.

targets.expr: sum by (method, route) (increase(http_request_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", app="catalogex", instance=~"$instance", route!~"/docs.*"}[$__range]))

(sum by (method, route) (increase(http_request_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", app="catalogex", instance=~"$instance", route!~"/docs.*", statusCode=~"4.."}[$__range])) or sum by (method, route) (increase(http_request_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", app="catalogex", instance=~"$instance", route!~"/docs.*"}[$__range])) * 0) / sum by (method, route) (increase(http_request_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", app="catalogex", instance=~"$instance", route!~"/docs.*"}[$__range]))

(sum by (method, route) (increase(http_request_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", app="catalogex", instance=~"$instance", route!~"/docs.*", statusCode=~"5.."}[$__range])) or sum by (method, route) (increase(http_request_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", app="catalogex", instance=~"$instance", route!~"/docs.*"}[$__range])) * 0) / sum by (method, route) (increase(http_request_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", app="catalogex", instance=~"$instance", route!~"/docs.*"}[$__range]))
histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, method, route) (increase(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", app="catalogex", instance=~"$instance", route!~"/docs.*"}[$__range])))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, method, route) (increase(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", app="catalogex", instance=~"$instance", route!~"/docs.*"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Responses by status code (selected range)
panels.description: Estimated responses per HTTP status code in the selected range: 2xx green, 4xx orange, 5xx red. Codes with no counted responses in the range are hidden. A 404 can be an expected product-not-found, a stale ID, or an unknown path; check the route table.

panels.title: Requests per second by route
panels.description: Request rate per method and route template, summed across pods. Gaps mean no matching series; 0 means series exist but no requests arrived. Read this beside the duration panel.

targets.expr: sum by (method, route) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{namespace="$namespace", app="catalogex", instance=~"$instance", route!~"/docs.*"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: p95 server-side request duration by route
panels.description: 95th percentile of server-side duration per method and route, combined across pods before the percentile is computed. It is estimated from buckets (5 ms, 10 ms, 25 ms, 50 ms, 100 ms, ...); values below 5 ms only mean "under 5 ms". Gaps mean no requests in that window. With sparse traffic, a point may reflect one or two requests.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, method, route) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", app="catalogex", instance=~"$instance", route!~"/docs.*"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Responses per second by status code
panels.description: Response rate per HTTP status code, stacked: 2xx green, 4xx orange, 5xx red.

panels.title: Recent requests
panels.description: The most recent traced API requests. Open a trace to see its database spans. Health checks, /metrics, and /docs are not traced.

panels.title: Failed requests (5xx)
panels.description: Traced requests whose server span has an error status, which the HTTP instrumentation sets for 5xx responses. 4xx responses are not errors here.

panels.title: Slow requests (over $slow_threshold)
panels.description: Traced requests slower than the selected threshold. The threshold is a provisional investigation filter, not an SLO: every server-side duration observed so far was under 50 ms.

panels.title: Database queries (slowest first)
panels.description: Recent PostgreSQL query spans from API requests, sorted by duration. Each row links to its trace. The readiness check query is excluded.

panels.title: CPU usage
panels.description: CPU time used per second by each process, in cores (1 = one full core).

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: RSS is all memory the process holds in RAM. The V8 heap (JavaScript objects) is part of it; heap total is the reserved heap and heap used is the occupied part. No limit is shown because no reliable limit metric is available.

panels.title: Event-loop lag (sampled)
panels.description: Event-loop delay reported at scrape time. prom-client resets its measurement on every collection, and two Prometheus servers scrape this pod. Each sample here therefore covers only the time since the previous scrape by either server, and a spike seen only by the other server is missing.
